title: CD44 exerts context-dependent control of subtype plasticity in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
summary: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity and phenotypic plasticity, primarily represented by the Classical-like and Basal-like subtypes. CD44 has been implicated in tumor progression and metastasis, but its context-dependent functions across PDAC subtypes remain poorly understood. In this study, CD44 was deleted using CRISPR/Cas9 in the Basal-like PDAC cell line MIA-PACA2 and the Classical-like PDAC cell line CFPAC1. RNA sequencing was performed to characterize the transcriptional consequences of CD44 loss in each subtype. This dataset provides a comprehensive resource for investigating the subtype-specific functions of CD44 and the molecular mechanisms underlying PDAC subtype plasticity.
overall_design: RNA-seq profiling of wildtype Mia-Paca2 and CFPAC1 cells and their CD44 knockout derivative

title: MIA-CTR1
extract_protocol_ch1: Retinas were removed, flash frozen on dry ice, and RNA was harvested using Trizol reagent. Illumina TruSeq RNA Sample Prep Kit (Cat#FC-122-1001) was used with 1 ug of total RNA for the construction of sequencing libraries.
RNA libraries were prepared for sequencing using standard Illumina protocols
data_processing: Illumina Casava1.7 software used for basecalling.

Sequenced reads were trimmed for adaptor sequence, and masked for low-complexity or low-quality sequence, then mapped to mm8 whole genome using bowtie v0.12.2 with parameters -q -p 4 -e 100 -y -a -m 10 --best --strata

Reads Per Kilobase of exon per Megabase of library size (RPKM) were calculated using a protocol from Chepelev et al., Nucleic Acids Research, 2009. In short, exons from all isoforms of a gene were merged to create one meta-transcript. The number of reads falling in the exons of this meta-transcript were counted and normalized by the size of the meta-transcript and by the size of the library.
Assembly: mm9
Supplementary files format and content: Matrix table with raw gene counts for every gene and every sample
